ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Your win rate is lying to you.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors chase 60%, 70%, even 80% win rates. Higher is better, right? Not necessarily. A bettor hitting 60% on -200 favorites is losing money. A bettor at 52% on +150 dogs is printing it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: ROI measures what you actually keep per dollar wagered. Win rate ignores the price you paid to win. Those are two completely different numbers, and only one of them shows up in your bank account.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: Bettor A goes 60-40 at -200 average odds. Net: roughly -8 units. Bettor B goes 52-48 at +150 average odds. Net: roughly +14 units. Same sample size. Bettor B wins less often and makes more money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: 54.1% win rate, +9.3% ROI, +45.4u across 53 days. The win rate is ordinary. The ROI is where the real number lives.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate is a vanity stat. ROI is the one that actually matters. 499 picks in. +45.4u. The math is public.
